feedback.problem:
Let
$C=[\begin{aligned}1 & -\sqrt{2} & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 2 & -5 & -7\end{aligned}]$
and
$D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & -5 \\ -3 & \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}].$
What are the dimensions of $CD?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We notice that $C$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $D$ is a $3\times 2$ matrix. 

There are $3$ columns in $C$ and $3$ rows in $D.$ Since the number of columns in $C$ equals the number of rows in $D,$ the matrices $C$ and $D$ are conformable for multiplication. 

The product $CD$ has dimensions $3\times 2:$ 

$$
{C}_{3\times \boxed{\text{3}}}{\times }_{✓}{D}_{\boxed{\text{3}}\times 2}={CD}_{3\times 2}
$$
